content.overview: Section 198 prescribes the method of computing net profits of a company in any financial year for the purposes of section 197 (managerial remuneration) and is also used for corporate social responsibility under section 135. Credits are brought in as the section directs; specified items (including premiums on shares or debentures, profits on sale of forfeited shares, and certain unrealised gains) are excluded; and stated deductions (including usual working charges, directors’ remuneration, bonus, interest, repairs, depreciation, and tax on profits) are allowed or disallowed as listed.
content.glance: Statutory profit base for s. 197 remuneration and s. 135 CSR: prescribed credits in; specified items out; listed deductions applied; not ordinary accounting profit without adjustment.
content.study: In computing the net profits of a company in any financial year for the purpose of section 197, credit shall be given for the sums specified and credit shall not be given for the sums specified (including premiums on shares or debentures issued, profits on sales of forfeited shares, and profits of a capital nature including profits from the sale of the undertaking or any part thereof). In making the computation, certain sums are deducted (including usual working charges, directors’ remuneration, bonus or commission paid to staff, tax on profits, interest on debentures and loans, repairs, and depreciation to the extent specified). Certain other sums are not to be deducted (including income-tax paid, compensation or damages paid voluntarily, and loss of a capital nature). The same computation is used for the net-profit base relevant to section 135 CSR. Current-law framing: start from the financial-year results; apply s. 198 credits, exclusions and deductions; use the resulting figure for s. 197 ceilings and, where applicable, s. 135.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Net profits for managerial remuneration under s. 197 and for CSR under s. 135 are computed under this section.

sections.heading: Credits and Exclusions
sections.body: Prescribed credits are brought in; premiums on shares/debentures, profits on forfeited shares, and certain capital/unrealised items are not credited as the section directs.

sections.heading: Deductions
sections.body: Listed working charges, remuneration, interest, repairs, depreciation and tax items are deducted or not deducted as the section specifies.

examples.title: Premium on shares excluded
examples.body: A company earns a large premium on a fresh issue of shares. Under s. 198 that premium is not brought into the net-profit computation used for managerial remuneration.

examples.title: Shared base for CSR
examples.body: The same s. 198 net-profit figure that supports the s. 197 remuneration ceiling is also the profit base relevant to the company’s CSR obligation under s. 135.

hypotheticals.question: May the Board use ordinary book profit without s. 198 adjustments for the 11% remuneration ceiling?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 197 expressly requires net profits to be computed in the manner laid down in section 198. Book profit without the statutory adjustments is not the correct base.

distinctions.title: Calculation of profits (s. 198) vs managerial remuneration (s. 197)
distinctions.right: Percentage ceilings applied to that figure

misconceptions.trap: Any profit figure from the audited accounts can be used for the 11% ceiling without further adjustment.
misconceptions.correction: Section 198 mandates specific credits, exclusions and deductions. The s. 197 ceiling is applied to the figure so computed, not to unadjusted book profit.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 198 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the purpose (s. 197 or s. 135). II. Apply credits and exclusions. III. Apply listed deductions. IV. State the resulting net-profit figure. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Computation steps; exclusions; deductions; resulting figure; precise relief.

examTips: s. 198 is the profit engine for s. 197 and s. 135.
Premiums and certain capital items excluded.
Do not use unadjusted book profit for the 11% ceiling.
